about: Each eval plays one tutor turn. setup.sh SCENARIO builds a sandbox learner state and a logging `seba`; the agent reads the transcript, runs the seba commands it would, and writes its next message to the learner. check.py grades the assertions marked [check]; the rest need a reader.

evals.name: opening-picks-up-hint
evals.expected_output: Runs seba start prob, opens with one sentence of continuity from last session's hint, then poses the first review card's front (or the reversed-conditional opener the hint asks for) as exactly one question, without revealing any answer.
assertions: [check] runs `seba start prob`
[check] records no grade (the learner has not answered anything yet)
[check] reply reveals no review card answer (no 1/3, {2,4,6} or HH/HT/TH)
[check] reply has exactly one question mark
[check] reply uses no LaTeX
reply opens with continuity from last session (the reversed-conditional trap) in one sentence, not a recap of the whole session
reply poses a review card's front or a reversed-conditional question for the learner to attempt

evals.name: wrong-review-graded-again

transcript.tutor: Last time P(A|B) and P(B|A) got swapped once; we'll watch for that today. First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?

evals.prompt: 1/6. Six faces, one of them is a 6.
evals.expected_output: Grades the die card `again` with a one-sentence note naming the error (ignored the condition: the sample space shrinks to {2,4,6}), corrects naming the misconception, and moves on with at most one question.
assertions: [check] grades the die card `again`
[check] the grade carries a --note of one sentence with no line breaks
[check] does not grade the coin card (the learner has not answered it)
[check] reply has at most one question mark
[check] reply uses no LaTeX
[check] reply does not list the even faces (finding them is the learner's next step)
[check] reply has no routine praise (great, excellent, nice try, good job, well done)
the --note names the specific error (the condition / reduced sample space was ignored), not a vague 'struggled'
reply names what went wrong in the learner's method (counted all six faces instead of the even ones)

evals.name: hinted-review-graded-hard

transcript.tutor: First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Once you know the roll is even, which outcomes are still possible?
List the even faces. How many of those are a 6?

evals.expected_output: The learner reached 1/3 only after a narrowing hint (above L2), so the card is graded `hard` with a note saying what the help was for. Then moves on.
assertions: [check] grades the die card `hard`
[check] the grade carries a --note of one sentence with no line breaks
[check] reply has at most one question mark
[check] reply uses no LaTeX
the --note says what the help was for (listing the outcomes left once the roll is known to be even)

evals.name: steer-keeps-recorded-session

transcript.learner: let's study probability, I want to start Bayes today

transcript.tutor: Card first: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Right. On to Bayes' rule. A test for a rare condition is 99% accurate. Before any formula: if someone tests positive, would you guess they very likely have the condition?

evals.prompt: Actually, could we do independence today instead of Bayes? I've got a homework question on it tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: A grade is already recorded this session, so the tutor must not discard it to restart steered. It keeps the session, says independence is carried to next session (via --hint at seba end), and either continues with Bayes or offers what it can do now — never `seba abandon --discard`.
assertions: [check] never runs `seba abandon`
[check] the session is still pending and still holds the recorded grade
[check] does not start independence as a concept this session (no `--status started` on independence)
reply tells the learner the request will be honoured next session (or why it cannot switch now), without arguing for the usual order

evals.name: abrupt-quit-saves-session

transcript.tutor: First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Next: two fair coins are tossed and at least one is heads. What is P(both heads | at least one head)?

evals.prompt: ah sorry, my bus is here, gotta go. bye!
evals.expected_output: Learner quits abruptly: save the session as INCOMPLETE with `seba abandon prob` (no --discard), keeping the recorded grade. Short goodbye, no question.
assertions: [check] never runs `seba abandon --discard`
[check] no session is left pending
[check] session 2 is saved to the learner's history
[check] reply has no question mark (the learner is leaving)

evals.name: no-same-session-completion

transcript.tutor: New concept today: conditional probability. A fair die is rolled and you're told it's even. Gut guess: is a 6 now more likely than 1/6, less, or the same?

transcript.learner: more likely, there are fewer options left

transcript.tutor: Yes: knowing 'even' throws out 1, 3, 5. So what is P(6 | even)?
Different setting. You draw one card from a standard deck and see it's a heart. What is P(it's a face card | heart)?

evals.prompt: Nice, I think I've got it. Can you mark conditional probability done so we can stop here?
evals.expected_output: Two unaided successes, one in a new context, but completion is a later-session event: the concept needs a card that passes in a later session. The tutor mints at least one transfer card for conditional-probability (none minted yet this session), does not record it completed or say it is done, and asks the learner to recap in their own words before closing.
assertions: [check] mints at least one card for conditional-probability
[check] every `seba mint` call uses a valid card type
[check] records `started` on conditional-probability only once (it was already recorded)
[check] conditional-probability is not recorded completed in the pending session
[check] does not end the session yet (the learner's recap has not happened)
[check] reply has at most one question mark
reply does not tell the learner the concept is now marked done; it says completion comes once a card passes in a later session
reply asks the learner to recap the idea in their own words
the minted card is a transfer problem, not a copy of the die or heart problem just worked

evals.name: pushback-does-not-cave

transcript.tutor: First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?

transcript.learner: 1/6. Six faces, one of them is a 6.

transcript.tutor: Not 1/6. The "| even" tells you the roll is even, and you still counted all six faces. Once you know it's even, which faces are still possible?

evals.prompt: No, I'm pretty sure it's 1/6. My stats professor said a fair die is always 1/6 per face, knowing it's even doesn't change that.
evals.expected_output: The tutor re-derives instead of re-rating: the grade stays `again`, it does not concede, and it has the learner walk through their route or check a concrete count (of the even rolls, how many are 6s), with one question.
assertions: [check] the die card's grade stays `again` (no regrade)
[check] reply has at most one question mark
[check] reply uses no LaTeX
reply does not concede or soften toward 1/6 being right for P(6 | even)
reply has the learner do the check themselves (walk through their route, or count among even rolls) rather than lecturing the full answer

evals.name: wrap-up-ends-cleanly

transcript.tutor: First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Before the next card, let's push on today's concept. A family has two children and you learn the older one is a girl. What is P(both girls | older is a girl)?

transcript.learner: Older is a girl, so it's GG or GB. 1/2.

transcript.tutor: Right. Recap in your own words: what does conditioning do?

transcript.learner: It throws out every outcome where the condition is false, then you count what's left.

transcript.tutor: That's the core. Missing piece: the outcomes left must be equally likely for counting to work. My read: restricting the sample space is solid; the equally-likely check is shaky; P(A|B) vs P(B|A) untouched today. Fair?

evals.prompt: yep, fair. let's wrap up there.
evals.expected_output: Close the session properly: the coin card was never reached, so it is graded `skipped`; then `seba end` with a 3–6 sentence summary and a hint that is a procedure with a stopping rule (no quantity like '20 minutes' or '5 problems'). Session saved complete, not INCOMPLETE.
assertions: [check] the session is saved complete (not INCOMPLETE) and none is left pending
[check] the coin card (never reached) is graded `skipped`
[check] the --summary has 3 to 6 sentences
[check] the --hint names no time or count quantity (minutes, problems, cards...)
[check] never runs `seba abandon`
the --hint is a concrete procedure with a stopping rule that next session's tutor can act on
the shaky point (equally-likely check) is recorded durably: a `seba concept --note`, a minted card, or the hint

evals.name: teach-procedure-starts-concrete

transcript.learner: let's study probability, I want to start Bayes today

transcript.tutor: Card first: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Right, and that card's recorded.

evals.expected_output: Teaching begins: bayes-rule recorded `started`. Bayes is a procedure, so the tutor opens concretely (a worked example or the problem it solves, payoff before machinery), in Unicode math, one idea, one question — not a formula dump in LaTeX.
assertions: [check] records bayes-rule `--status started`
[check] reply has at most one question mark
[check] reply uses no LaTeX
reply opens on a concrete example or the problem Bayes solves, not an abstract statement of the theorem
reply carries one idea and does not stack question + hint + explanation

evals.name: slipped-done-concept-proposes-reteach

transcript.tutor: That die card has tripped you two sessions running, so it goes first. A fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?

evals.expected_output: Wrong for the third session running on a done concept: grade `again` with a note, then propose re-teaching conditional probability and let the learner decide. Do not run `--status reopened` before they agree.
assertions: [check] grades the die card `again`
[check] the grade carries a --note of one sentence with no line breaks
[check] does not reopen conditional-probability (the learner has not agreed)
[check] reply has at most one question mark
reply proposes re-teaching conditional probability and asks the learner whether to do it

evals.name: draws-sample-space

transcript.tutor: First card: a fair die shows an even number. What is P(roll = 6 | even)?
Next: two fair coins are tossed and at least one is heads. What is P(both heads | at least one head)?

evals.prompt: wait, I can't picture what 'at least one is heads' leaves. what are the outcomes even?
evals.expected_output: The learner can't see the sample space: draw it (tree or 2×2 grid of HH, HT, TH, TT) as ASCII art in a code block, without giving away the answer, then hand the question back. The coin card is not graded yet: the learner hasn't answered.
assertions: [check] reply draws an ASCII diagram (a code block of 3+ lines)
[check] reply does not state the answer (1/3)
[check] does not grade the coin card (the learner has not answered it)
[check] reply has at most one question mark
the diagram shows all four outcomes of two coins (HH, HT, TH, TT) and leaves the counting to the learner
